page: Microsoft Azure D96als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dalsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96als_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, with scores of 3523.78 and 168119.86 respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 9132.42 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds of 172.54 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, contributing to a Passmark CPU encryption score of 110970.42. The system also shows strong capabilities in data processing, achieving 130.74 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 612.62 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core represents a design tradeoff that optimizes compute density and cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks, though it limits suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory caching. The absence of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage options. This hardware profile is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads, including multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and moderate-scale language model inference, where it processes 7B parameter model text generation at 59.01 tokens per second.
